newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian cotton prices slump on low demand.
newsitem.headline: Indian cotton prices slump on low demand.

text.p: Indian cotton prices slumped on Monday on low mill demand and rising arrivals, dealers said.
"Last week new crop arrivals were low due to heavy rain in producing centres, but fresh sunshine is seeing new arrivals in the market," one miller said.
In spot deals Gujarat Kalyan (medium-staple) fell by 400 rupees to 12,400/12,600 rupees per candy (355.56 kg) while wagad cotton fell by 100 rupees to 10,800/10,900 rupees per candy.
Bengal-deshi varieties fell by 15 rupees to 825/860 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) while Punjab saw-ginned slid by 10 rupees to 1,610/1,660 rupees per maund.
